rv.q: He is verbally (“prologue” mispronounced prow-log-wee) and physically energetic: his slapstick gymnastics in the often lumberingly unfunny Pyramus and Thisbe playlet stop the show with earned applause.
But that is just picking holes in what is a fresh and vibrant Dream with genuine wit and warmth from its high-octane start to its absurd finish.
Chichester Festival Theatre have fantastically interwoven the politics, parties, and plights of this era of British history into The Bard’s comedy of conflict, romance, and magic.
I simply didn't buy into the full evening here and believe I gave it fair attention.
